note: BRCA-deficient xenografts and PAR pharmacodynamic models for veliparib, niraparib and rucaparib predicted tumour PAR loss, dose and BRCA-selective activity; patients matched on all four questions.
label: Ovarian cancer (PARP1/2)

engagement.model: Human tumour xenografts, needle-biopsy PAR ELISA (veliparib)
engagement.note: Single veliparib doses cut intratumour PAR >95% in mouse xenografts; the assay and biopsy design were built for the first-in-human trial.
engagement.quote: A single ABT-888 dose (3 or 12.5 mg/kg) reduced intratumor PAR levels by >95%.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMC full text available, not needed for the status).

engagement.model: Human tumour xenografts, needle-biopsy PAR ELISA (veliparib)
engagement.note: In the phase 0 trial the xenograft-qualified PAR assay showed significant PAR loss in patients' tumour biopsies and PBMCs at 25 and 50 mg. Retrodiction: patient PARP inhibition was public first (olaparib phase 1 PD-guided escalation, Yap ASCO 2007; Fong ASCO May 2008), before Kinders (Nov 2008).
engagement.short: PAR fell in patient tumour biopsies
engagement.quote: Statistically significant inhibition of poly (ADP-ribose) levels was observed in tumor biopsies and peripheral blood mononuclear cells at the 25-mg and 50-mg dose levels.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers; the earlier patient PD result is known from the Fong 2008 ASCO abstract, which names the PD-active dose but gives no PAR numbers.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Kinders 2008 model, Kummar 2009 patients); the two are companion NCI papers on one design, but neither abstract puts the numbers side by side. Patients had mixed advanced cancers, not ovarian only; engagement does not need the context's disease. PAR is PARP's own product, so readout_tier proximal. NCT00387608 (phase 0, start 2006-06) has no posted results. Ruling (retrodiction by post-dating, engagement counts any drug on the target): Fong 2008 ASCO abstract 5510 (doi 10.1200/jco.2008.26.15_suppl.5510, 2008-05-20) reports dose escalation 'guided by ... pharmacodynamic (PD) data' and 'Once a PD active dose was identified'; Kinders 2008 was first public 2008-11, so same -> retro.

dose.note: Niraparib (MK-4827) was well tolerated in mice and active as a single agent in a BRCA1-deficient xenograft; no human exposure yet. Its 'well tolerated' claim is scored in safety.
dose.quote: Compound 56 was well tolerated in vivo and demonstrated efficacy as a single agent in a xenograft model of BRCA-1 deficient cancer.

dose.note: FDA: the preclinical target (>50% PBMC PARP inhibition ~ 90% tumour inhibition) was exceeded above 80 mg/day; 300 mg/day then won NOVA.
dose.short: PBMC PARP target exceeded above 80 mg
dose.quote: The evidence for this endpoint was based on preclinical data suggesting that greater than 50% inhibition of PARP activity in circulating PBMCs correlates with 90% inhibition of PARP activity within tumor tissues and anti-proliferative effects.
dose.confidence_note: Bundle text of the review read (clin-pharm section, pp. 10-15 to 10-22).
dose.reason: Preclinical PD target reached in patients
dose.judgement: Target reached and the drug worked (NOVA, efficacy cell), so same. Sandhu 2013 (doi 10.1016/S1470-2045(13)70240-7; NCT00749502, no posted results) first reported PARP inhibition >50% above 80 mg/day, but the link to the preclinical threshold is stated only in the 2017 review, so the entry dates there. margin_stated false: no nonclinical document stated the effective exposure was tolerated; 300 mg/day caused grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia in 34% of NOVA patients and most needed dose reductions (PRIMA later moved to weight/platelet-based 200 mg), which the reviewer judged manageable; no stated margin, so it is not scored as a dose failure.
dose.magnitude_basis: PBMC PARP inhibition threshold vs dose
dose.population: Advanced solid tumours; recurrent ovarian cancer

dose.note: A decision-tree model of NOVA patients predicted that body weight <77 kg or platelets <150,000/uL should start niraparib at 200 mg without losing efficacy.
dose.quote: The analysis presented suggests that patients with baseline body weight of <77 kg or baseline platelets of <150 000/µl may benefit from a starting dose of 200 mg/day.
dose.judgement: A model fitted to NOVA patient data, not a preclinical system; in scope as an in-silico model used to choose dose. Its prediction (per-patient starting dose) was tested prospectively, so it is not a retrodiction.
dose.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer (NOVA safety population)
dose.model: Decision-tree / exposure-safety model of NOVA patients (niraparib individualized starting dose)

dose.note: NORA dosed 249 patients by the weight/platelet rule (235 at 200 mg); PFS benefit held regardless of BRCA status and toxicity was manageable.
dose.short: NORA: 200 mg ISD effective and safer
dose.quote: Individualized niraparib dosing is effective and safe and should be considered standard practice in this setting.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NORA has no fixed-dose comparator; PRIMA's stated fixed- vs individualized-dose comparison (Mirza 2023, doi 10.1002/cncr.34706) agrees.
dose.judgement: Paired by me (Berek 2018 model, NORA 2021 trial). Mirza 2023 states the comparison in PRIMA: 'similar dose intensity, similar efficacy, and improved safety were observed with the ISD compared with the FSD regimen'; it changes no status. The model stated 200 mg was effective and better tolerated, and patients dosed to it showed that, so margin_stated true. NCT03705156 has no posted results; FDA adopted the ISD in the 2020 label (PRIMA review not read).
dose.magnitude_basis: PFS benefit and haematologic toxicity at the 200 mg individualized starting dose vs the model's predicted benefit
dose.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, China, BRCA-mutant and wild-type (NORA)
dose.model: Decision-tree / exposure-safety model of NOVA patients (niraparib individualized starting dose)

efficacy.note: Niraparib killed BRCA1/2-mutant cells at 10-100 nM, selectively over BRCA-proficient cells, and shrank a BRCA1-deficient xenograft.
efficacy.quote: the resulting PARP inhibitors display antiproliferation activities against BRCA-1 and BRCA-2 deficient cancer cells, with high selectivity over BRCA proficient cells.

efficacy.note: NOVA's primary endpoint: niraparib maintenance quadrupled PFS in gBRCA (21.0 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.27). Retrodiction: olaparib responses in BRCA ovarian cancer (Fong ASCO May 2008) predate Jones 2009. gBRCA OS later not significant (HR 0.85).
efficacy.quote: Patients in the niraparib group had a significantly longer median duration of progression-free survival than did those in the placebo group, including 21.0 vs. 5.5 months in the gBRCA cohort
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Jones 2009 (model) with NOVA (trial); NOVA does not compare itself with the xenografts. The gBRCA cohort is 100% biomarker-positive. Not neg: no member failed in BRCA/HRD ovarian cancer (veliparib, the weakest trapper per Murai 2012, still met VELIA's primary endpoint, Coleman 2019; rucaparib ARIEL3 and, outside FDA, pamiparib and senaparib were positive; not re-read here). Outside this population, the FDA-reviewed niraparib PDX study found HRD-negative models insensitive, while NOVA's HRD-negative subgroup still benefited (abstract: benefit regardless of HRD status); an Unselected context would score that differently. Ruling (retrodiction by post-dating; efficacy counts any drug on the target): Fong 2008 ASCO abstract 5510 (2008-05-20) reported 14 partial responses in 32 evaluable BRCA-deficient ovarian cancer patients on olaparib, and Fong 2009 NEJM (epub 2009-06-24) followed; Jones 2009 was first public 2009-10, so same -> retro. Checker adjudication applied: final gBRCA OS (Matulonis 2025, HR 0.85, n.s.) sets outcome_tested negative; status still follows PFS.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth inhibition vs PFS hazard ratio
efficacy.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, germline BRCA

patient_trials.quote: The primary end point was progression-free survival.
OS did not significantly differ between treatment arms.

efficacy.note: Rucaparib (AG014699) killed BRCA1/2-mutant and BRCA1-silenced cancer cells but not BRCA-proficient ones, and slowed growth of BRCA-mutant xenografts.
efficacy.quote: Growth of xenograft tumors with BRCA1/2 mutations or with epigenetically silenced BRCA1 was reduced by AG014699 treatment
efficacy.judgement: Rucaparib's own BRCA-deficient cell and xenograft model (breast, pancreatic lines), distinct from the niraparib track; opens at first publication.
efficacy.model: BRCA-deficient cancer cells and xenografts (rucaparib, AG014699)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour growth delay vs PFS in BRCA-mutant vs LOH-low tumours
efficacy.note: ARIEL2 Part 1, single-arm, primary endpoint PFS: BRCA-mutant tumours had median PFS 12.8 months vs 5.2 in LOH-low (HR 0.27). Single-arm design scored on its primary endpoint. Retrodiction: olaparib BRCA ovarian responses public 2008.
efficacy.quote: Median progression-free survival after rucaparib treatment was 12·8 months (95% CI 9·0-14·7) in the BRCA mutant subgroup, 5·7 months (5·3-7·6) in the LOH high subgroup, and 5·2 months (3·6-5·5) in the LOH low subgroup.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 27908594, epub 2016-11-29); ARIEL4 and its final OS from abstracts (PMIDs 35298906, 39914419).
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Drew 2011 (model) with ARIEL2 Part 1 (trial). Rulings: (1) single-arm trial with no success bar is scored on its primary endpoint (PFS) in the direction the model predicted, longer PFS in BRCA-mutant tumours, so a match; (2) rule 6 earliest date: ARIEL2 (epub 2016-11-29) is the track's first patient comparison, ahead of ARIEL3 (Coleman 2017 Lancet, NCT01968213, results posted 2018-08-03; checker's proposed 2017) and ARIEL4 (2022), which move to patient_trials; (3) retrodiction: Drew 2011 (epub 2010-12-23) post-dates olaparib's BRCA ovarian responses (Fong ASCO 2008; Fong 2009 NEJM), so retro. ARIEL4 final OS favoured chemotherapy (19.4 vs 25.4 months, HR 1.3), so outcome_tested stays negative.
efficacy.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent high-grade ovarian carcinoma, BRCA-mutant subgroup (ARIEL2 Part 1)

patient_trials.quote: Results from the ARIEL4 study support rucaparib as an alternative treatment option to chemotherapy for patients with relapsed, BRCA1-mutated or BRCA2-mutated ovarian carcinoma.
Median overall survival was 19·4 months (95% CI 15·2-23·6) in the rucaparib group versus 25·4 months (21·4-27·6) in the chemotherapy group

efficacy.model: BRCA-deficient cancer cells and xenografts (rucaparib, AG014699)

safety.note: FDA: rat/dog marrow and GI toxicity matched patients' cytopenias and GI effects; ALT/AST rises were absent in animals. Retrodiction: ARIEL2 reported rucaparib's anaemia and ALT rises first.
safety.short: Marrow toxicity matched; ALT rise missed
safety.quote: Overall, the findings in animals were consistent with the hematological and gastrointestinal adverse reactions reported in patients treated with rucaparib.
safety.confidence_note: Bundle text of the review read (pharm/tox executive summary).
safety.judgement: Partial: the next sentence states ALT/AST increases in patients were not seen in animal toxicology (label: ALT increase 74%, grade 3-4 13%, discontinuation 0.3%). Rats and dogs could have shown transaminase rises, so a strict reading would make this contra; I scored same + partial because the reviewer weighs it as a lab abnormality without hepatotoxicity and the dose-limiting harm (marrow) was predicted. MDS/AML could not be shown in 13-week studies; genotoxicity flagged it. No opening untested entry: no dated public source for the toxicology before the review. Ruling (retrodiction; safety counts only the same drug's earlier patient result): the toxicology was first public in the December 2016 review, after Swisher 2017 ARIEL2 (epub 2016-11-29) reported rucaparib's grade >=3 anaemia (22%) and ALT/AST elevations (12%), so same -> retro, still partial.
safety.magnitude_basis: target organs (marrow, GI) in animals vs adverse reactions in patients

safety.note: Niraparib raised dog BP and heart rate from 0.7x human unbound Cmax; patients had hypertension, grade 3-4 in 9%. Retrodiction: NOVA (2016) reported the hypertension first.
safety.quote: although these findings are consistent with adverse reactions reported in clinical trials with niraparib in patients receiving the recommended dose.
safety.confidence_note: Bundle text of the review read (pharm/tox executive summary); hypertension rate from the 2017 label. NOVA's hypertension rate is in the NEJM full text, not its abstract (not re-read).
safety.reason: Dog BP and marrow signals matched
safety.judgement: The dog safety-pharmacology study, not the repeat-dose toxicology, carries this prediction (model_change dropped: no preceding contra). The same review also states rat/dog marrow findings were consistent with niraparib's cytopenias. The dog rise began at 0.7x human unbound Cmax, so the margin is within 2x; the reviewer notes vagotomy may overstate it. Ruling (retrodiction; safety counts the same drug's earlier patient result): the dog study was first public in the 2017 review, after NOVA (Mirza 2016, epub 2016-10-08) reported niraparib hypertension, so same -> retro.
safety.magnitude_basis: unbound Cmax at first BP rise vs clinical unbound Cmax

safety.note: Passing tolerability claim, now a safety prediction: niraparib was well tolerated in mice at doses active in a BRCA1-deficient xenograft.
safety.quote: Compound 56 was well tolerated in vivo and demonstrated efficacy as a single agent in a xenograft model of BRCA-1 deficient cancer.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 19873981); the tolerability readout (body weight, clinical signs) is not stated in the abstract.
safety.judgement: Opener for the niraparib xenograft track in safety under the ruling that a 'well tolerated' statement in an efficacy paper is a scored safety prediction.

safety.magnitude_basis: tolerability in mice at efficacious doses vs grade 3-4 haematologic toxicity in patients
safety.note: Mice tolerated efficacious niraparib; at 300 mg/day NOVA patients had grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia (33.8%), anaemia (25.3%) and neutropenia (19.6%).
safety.quote: The most common grade 3 or 4 adverse events that were reported in the niraparib group were thrombocytopenia (in 33.8%), anemia (in 25.3%), and neutropenia (in 19.6%), which were managed with dose modifications.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers; mice can show myelosuppression, so the silence is scorable.
safety.judgement: Paired by me (Jones 2009 model, NOVA trial). Ruling: a passing tolerability claim is a safety prediction. Mice can show cytopenias, and ovarian cancer patients dosed at the effective 300 mg/day had frequent grade 3-4 marrow toxicity, so contra. Not a retrodiction: niraparib's own first patient safety data (Sandhu, ASCO 2010) came after Jones 2009. Sandhu 2013 (mixed solid tumours) showed grade 4 thrombocytopenia earlier, but NOVA is the first measurement in this disease's patients.
safety.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer (NOVA safety population)
